user.title: Spot Forecast
user.description: Forecasts day-ahead electricity prices for the next days. Prices come from Energy-Charts and weather from Open-Meteo; no account or API key is needed.

data_description.zone: Day-ahead market zone whose prices are forecast.

abort.already_configured: This bidding zone is already set up.

data_description.surcharge: Gross amount per kWh for the total-price sensor and the forecast card's view with fees, in EUR/kWh (grid fees, levies, taxes, VAT included; enter it as you pay it). The total price is the market price plus VAT (next option) plus this amount. 0 removes the total-price sensor. The price sensor, the statistics and the peak and negative-price sensors stay on the market price.
data_description.vat: VAT in percent charged on the market price for the total price: market price × (1 + VAT/100) + grid fees and taxes. The default is the zone's standard rate: 19 in Germany, 21 in the Netherlands, 25 in Denmark. Luxembourg charges a different rate on electricity: enter the one on your bill.
data_description.peak_threshold: Wholesale price at or above which an hour counts as a price peak, in ct/kWh without taxes or grid fees. The default comes from the model's training data.
data_description.backfill_days: How many past days of forecasts are reconstructed on first start so accuracy statistics have history. 0 turns backfill off.
data_description.auto_update: Once a day, download a newer forecast model for this zone when one is published. It is used only if it fits this version of the integration and passes its checks.

model_outdated.title: Spot Forecast model is outdated
model_outdated.description: The forecast model {version} was trained on data up to {cutoff}, more than {max_age} days ago. Forecasts get less accurate as the market changes. Turn on automatic model updates in the options, or update the Spot Forecast integration, to get a newer model.

model_future.title: Spot Forecast model is dated in the future
model_future.description: The forecast model {version} says it was trained on data up to {cutoff}, more than {max_ahead} days after today. Check the date and time of the Home Assistant host. If they are right, the model file is wrong: update the Spot Forecast integration.
